verdict.line: You lose if Renekton gets a clean Q-E-W all-in before level 6; you win if you survive to your E-R spike and out-scale with Trinity-Hydra.

brief.thesis: Camille has no dash until E (Hookshot) unlocks at level 6, so for the first five levels she is trading into a champion whose entire kit is built around forcing that exact window — Renekton's Slice and Dice (E) closes distance for free and his Fury system rewards every auto and ability he lands on you. The 47.9% win rate over 733 games reflects a lane you survive, not one you win outright, before you flip it with items and E-R access.

theirWindow.what: At 50 Fury his Q (Cull the Meek) heals him hard on hit and his W (Ruthless Predator) stuns — if he's sitting on 50+ Fury and walks up with E (Slice and Dice), assume the stun-auto-Q combo is coming and play for the shield proc off P (Adaptive Defenses) instead of trading back.

yourWindow.when: His E whiffs, or R (Dominus) is down
yourWindow.what: A whiffed first-cast E leaves him with no second dash and no gap-closer for roughly 6 seconds — punish immediately with Q (Precision Protocol) into auto-weaves. Post-6, his ultimate is both his burst and his sustain; once it's on cooldown he has no healing tool, so that's when you commit to extended trades.

start.why: This is a defensive-shape matchup — the flat damage reduction on minion/champion poke and the passive heal let you hold CS through Renekton's auto-heavy trades. It's the measured pick at 47.9% over 261 games and matches the reality that you're absorbing pressure, not initiating it, before level 6.

boots.why: Renekton's whole early kit is autos plus on-hit-adjacent abilities layered on top of an engage; the flat reduction directly blunts his all-in burst. 80.7% pick rate and the standard choice into an AD auto-attacker.

core.why: The spellblade proc plus movement speed is what finally lets you close and kite Renekton once your E is live — this is the item that flips the matchup from level 10 onward.
Sustain and AoE clear to offset the early lane deficit and start winning extended trades once he's out of Fury-fueled heal windows.
Highest-performing third item at 55.5% over 173 games — the damage-over-time conversion is specifically strong against a burst-into-all-in champion like Renekton.

situational.when: you're behind or he's snowballed and you need to survive his all-in rather than win the trade outright
you're ahead and want faster E-Q cooldowns to chain resets in extended skirmishes
the lane is stuck on a slow, contested wave and you need the AoE clear component before finishing Hydra

runes.keystoneWhy: You can't out-trade Renekton levels 1-5, so Grasp's max-health proc and the free sustain from every auto you land keeps your HP bar level with his instead of bleeding out to his Fury-fueled combo.

summoners.why: This combo posts the best measured result in the data (52.2% over 19.7% pick share). Given the defensive shape of the lane, Teleport lets you reset after losing an early trade or crash a wave and TP back in, rather than committing Ignite to fights you're not favoured to win before 6.

playing.title: Play the wave, not the champion
playing.detail: Levels 1-5, don't extend trades — use W (Tactical Sweep) at max range to poke and farm without walking into his E engage range. Freeze near your tower when possible to remove his free all-in angle.

playing.title: Bait the first E before you commit
playing.detail: Force him to use Slice and Dice to engage rather than walking up yourself. If it hits nothing, he has no second dash and no gap-closer for several seconds — that's your punish window.

playing.title: Track Fury, not just health
playing.detail: A Renekton at 30 Fury is far less dangerous than one at 50+. Watch the bar under his portrait; below the empower threshold his Q and W lose their extra effects entirely.

playing.title: Don't fight through his R
playing.detail: Dominus heals him off missing health and grants tenacity — if he pops it mid-trade, disengage rather than trading through it. Re-engage once it's on cooldown.

playing.title: Level 6 is your first real all-in
playing.detail: Use E (Hookshot) onto terrain to reposition onto him or onto him directly if in range, then R (The Hextech Ultimatum) to lock the fight in place before he can E away.

playing.title: Itemize around his damage type
playing.detail: He's 100% physical — Plated Steelcaps and eventually Death's Dance are doing real work here, not just generic stat sticks.

playing.title: Shift the win condition post-10
playing.detail: Once Trinity Force is up, stop playing for survival and start looking for picks with E-R; your kit out-scales his flat Fury payoff.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the timing breakdown, power spikes, and trade-pattern reasoning are my own tactical read of the two kits.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Renekton using his (E) to close in to deal damage one-sidedly! Although it is difficult to contest lane early game, try using Camille’s shield [P] and regen[W] to ease the early lane process!
